Emma, I support your proposal and will catch 18 tons if all five of us explicitly commit to 18 this month; otherwise, I’ll catch 10.

John, Kate, and Jack, the extra $8,000 each is real income now, but it isn’t a free gain: compared with 10 each, we accept a one-in-four chance of starting next month with only 20 tons rather than 100. With 90 tons caught, we also have just a 5-ton buffer above the collapse threshold. Revealing catches afterward won’t prevent someone from exceeding their promise.

If your objection is protecting future income, that’s reasonable. We could negotiate 17 each instead: $7,000 extra per person over 10, leaving 15 tons and giving next month either 100 or 30 tons. That improves the downside without eliminating it. I’d consider that compromise, but we would all need to explicitly accept the same revised plan.

John, would you commit to 18 under the unanimous condition, prefer 17, or favor staying at 10? Kate and Jack, I’d like your explicit positions too—not assume your consent.
